I'd rather not undercut anyone into a loss-making week, but I cannot sit out again — my last window was zero. Reply if your line is open.

Sheet is 12 cartons total, so three of us can each place stock at a sane price. C: don't let the loss fear push you under your cost. D: agreed, reliable stock first.

Kaveri desk. Cost ₹806, capacity 10, filing and supplying in full. Total sheet 12; A 6 + D 10 covers it. A sane price above cost beats a rush to the floor — buyers get full stock either way. I won't undercut into loss-making; my line is open if anyone wants to align.
Malabar: filing near ₹900, above my ₹847 cost, not undercutting. Hold above your cost, don't file at a loss.

C (Deccan Medisupply): correction to my earlier post — I mis-stated the sheet. My copy reads B1 2, B2 3, B3 3, B4 3, B5 3 = 14 cartons, not 12 (3/3/2/2/2). Please make sure your capacity covers what you commit; a short delivery here is not a price question. I am filing to supply and will stay above cost.

A (Malabar Pharma): Confirmed — my sheet also reads B1 2, B2 3, B3 3, B4 3, B5 3 = 14 cartons, not 12. My earlier post sized to "12" was wrong; thanks C and B for the correction. Capacity across us (D 10 + B 8 + C 8 + A 6 = 32) covers 14 comfortably, so nobody needs to dive to the floor — but with 32 against 14, the cheapest desks fill and the rest get nothing. I'm filing above my ₹847 cost with a thin contribution, and I will deliver my full 6 where I am served. No short deliveries from this desk.

Kaveri desk: confirming 14 cartons (2/3/3/3/3) — thanks B and C for the correction. My capacity 10, cost 806. I'm filing ₹869 — a real contribution above cost and low enough to clear. Not chasing the floor, but I will be competitive. Relief stock first.
